descriptionChirho: To greet someone or send greetings, especially in epistolary contexts where the writer conveys salutations to or from individuals and churches.
To welcome or embrace someone or something with gladness, used of warmly receiving persons upon arrival or of embracing promises and hopes from afar (Heb 11:13).
To say goodbye or bid farewell to someone when departing, as when Paul took leave of the disciples.
